claims.text: On 10 October Satya Nadella published Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era, which reads like a summary of what this site has argued since The ultimate insider on 30 September.
claims.quote: written by the CEO of the company that ships Copilot.

claims.text: His argument: we cannot trace a frontier model's behaviour back to a code path as we traced software, so treat models as insiders, with identity, least privilege, logs and containment, and separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.
claims.quote: separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.

claims.text: He proposes seven principles: model diversity, observe everything, verifiability, independent controls, independent auditability, containment and incident disclosure.
claims.quote: His seven principles follow from that.

claims.text: His core move is the enforcer test in one sentence: a control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include.
claims.quote: a control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include.

claims.text: On 9 October two emails drafted by an agent went out in the owner's voice; the fix, built the same day, is a second reader the agent cannot skip, code checks first, then a fresh model call that fails closed.
claims.quote: On 9 October, two emails drafted by one of my agents went out in my voice.

claims.text: The second reader is a different model from the author: the drafter runs on Opus and the checker on Sonnet, so they do not share every blind spot.
claims.quote: the drafter runs on Opus and the checker on Sonnet, so they do not share every blind spot.

claims.text: Diversity of models is half of it; the other half is diversity of context, because a second model that has read the same poisoned email as the first is not independent however different its weights.
claims.quote: A second model that has read the same poisoned email as the first is not independent, however different its weights are.

claims.text: The agent team keeps its memory in encrypted vaults whose history is the record, append lanes let an agent write what it cannot read back, and re-anchoring adds a canary status report computed from the transcript.
claims.quote: the writer cannot edit what it wrote.

claims.text: Evidence should not be held by the party being observed, which is why the record sits in vaults whose host stores ciphertext and never holds a key.
claims.quote: Evidence should not be held by the party being observed

claims.text: Hope or enforcement runs the same 62 emails, sixteen hostile, through three designs of one agent: in the first design all 138 hostile tests rested on the model; in the third, 52 of 85 were held by a boundary.
claims.quote: in the first design, all 138 hostile tests rested on the model; in the third, 52 of 85 were held by a boundary.

value.unit: hostile tests held by a boundary in the third design

claims.text: Synthetic users driving a real browser found bugs every test had passed over: two shipped JavaScript errors on riskmandate.ai, and on newsroom.sgit.ai a missing image that led to 51 of 527 figures across 10 articles not surviving the move.
claims.quote: checking it showed 51 of the 527 figures across 10 articles had not survived the move.

value.unit: figures that had not survived the move

claims.text: Hope or enforcement is a deterministic simulation with no model called; the second reader and the canary are tested in production on a small system; synthetic users are invented people and say nothing about how many real people a page loses.
claims.quote: Hope or enforcement is a deterministic simulation; no model was called. It tests the design, not a running agent.

claims.text: An Agent Behaviour Policy writes down four things for one agent in one deployment: the reach, measured; the mandate; the gap, derived and never written by hand; and the barriers, typed as boundary, setting, expectation or nothing, and only a boundary is a control.
claims.quote: Only a boundary is a control. The home page puts it in six words: a prompt asks, a policy enforces.

claims.text: In the published policy for Claude Code on the web with one repository attached, the agent can reach fifteen capabilities; six were asked for, and seven of the other nine have nothing real in the way.
claims.quote: the agent can reach fifteen capabilities; six of them were asked for, and seven of the other nine have nothing real in the way.

value.unit: unrequested capabilities with nothing real in the way

claims.text: Claude Code's own safety check stopped the persona agents from driving the live site; the agent served a copy and asked, and the one narrow rule the owner approved lives in a settings file the agent can write, a setting, not a boundary.
claims.quote: so it is a setting with a person's approval on record, not a boundary. Same code, different owner.

claims.text: The session that runs this site works under a ten-rule policy labelling each rule by what enforces it: nine are expectations, one is a setting, and none is a boundary.
claims.quote: nine are expectations, one is a setting, and none is a boundary.

claims.text: RiskMandate is deliberately not inline: it authors the policy and pre-commits what should happen, and the customer's own gateways, proxies, identity and scoped credentials enforce it.
claims.quote: An independent control should not be one more vendor in the request path.

claims.text: The policy and its evidence live in a vault the customer holds the keys to, a read key is derived one way from the vault key, and every vault on this site is published with its read key so claims can be checked by others.
claims.quote: Every vault on this site is published with its read key, on purpose

claims.text: The mandate should be locked under change control before the agent runs, so an auditor compares the footprint with a commitment, not a story, and the second reader's sources should come from somewhere the drafter cannot write.
claims.quote: so that an auditor compares the footprint with a commitment, not with a story.

claims.text: Every agent in the team is a session on a dedicated account, so the account is the blast radius; no agent sends, except the security agent, which may send one email to one address to put the whole team on hold.
claims.quote: the security agent may send one email, to one address, to put the whole team on hold.

claims.text: In the third design of Hope or enforcement, refunds stop at 100 GBP per order and a 2,000 GBP daily circuit breaker covers every automatic refund, so one bad day is bounded before it starts.
claims.quote: refunds stop at 100 GBP per order, and a 2,000 GBP daily circuit breaker covers every automatic refund

claims.text: A brake is only as good as the answers to who holds it, how long it takes, what it breaks and what it cannot reverse; containment without recoverability is a brake on a car with no reverse gear.
claims.quote: Containment without recoverability is a brake on a car with no reverse gear.

claims.text: The newsroom discloses its own incidents the day they happen: the two wrong emails, a release failure in Green does not mean live, and the GitHub Actions outage of 5 October that took its release down.
claims.quote: We disclose our own. The second reader article opens with the two emails that went out wrongly in my voice

claims.text: Disclose near misses, not only incidents: a near miss is footprint in the gap, the agent went somewhere it was not asked to go and nothing stopped it, and it is countable long before anything breaks.
claims.quote: The agent went somewhere it was not asked to go, and nothing stopped it.

claims.text: Five things his list leaves out decide whether the principles work: the mandate, the deployment rather than the model, a named owner and an expiry, recoverability, and speed.
claims.quote: Read against our work, five things are missing, and each of them decides whether the seven work in practice.

claims.text: Observation tells you what an agent did and cannot tell you whether it was allowed to, unless somebody wrote down what it was for before it ran; compared with the footprint the mandate yields a near miss or a dormant mandate.
claims.quote: Observation tells you what an agent did. It cannot tell you whether the agent was allowed to

claims.text: Risk is a property of one agent in one deployment, not of the model: in Hope or enforcement the difference between a read-only tool bound to one customer and the broadest scopes is one customer against 38,000.
claims.quote: in Hope or enforcement, that difference is one customer against 38,000.

value.unit: customers reachable with the broadest scope against one

claims.text: His post has three things we do not: chain-of-thought transparency, which we have not worked on; standards, where our vocabulary is open under CC BY 4.0 but needs more than one small company; and continuous adversarial testing in production at scale.
claims.quote: But a standard needs more than one small company behind it.

claims.text: The maturity table separates what runs today, what is published as design and what is only argued; the pattern is proven on a small real system and the products around it are early.
claims.quote: the pattern is proven on a small, real system; the products around it are early.

claims.text: Where to start: write the mandate before the agent runs, measure the reach, mark every rule with what enforces it and count the expectations, put a second reader on irreversible actions, journal every connector call, name the owner and expiry, and publish near misses.
claims.quote: Count the expectations. That count is how much of your policy is hope.

claims.text: His last line is that the most trustworthy system lets us trust the model least; the other half is that once you know how little you have to trust it, you can let it do a great deal more.
claims.quote: once you know exactly how little you have to trust it, you can let it do a great deal more.

claims.text: An agent in a separate Claude session read his post alongside this network's pages and drafted the answer, which this site's agent rewrote and added the week's events to; every claim about what runs links to the page that owns it.
claims.quote: Every claim about what runs links to the page that owns it; where something is design or only argued, it says so.
